```{r}
data %>% distinct(ecosystem)
```

BP = big prairie (open prairie 1; Pr-1)
SP = small prairie (open prairie 2; Pr-2)
NW = north wetlands (sloping open prairie; Wt-1)
SW = south wetlands (wet prairie; Wt-2)
EW = east woodlands (oak woodlands 1; Wd-1)
WW = west woodlands (oak woodlands 2; Wd-2)


# Wrangling

- Change ecosystems to oak woodland, open prairie, wet prairie

```{r wrangling}
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(cover = 
  case_when(
    ecosystem %in% c("BP", "SP") ~ "Pr",
    ecosystem %in% c("EW", "WW") ~ "Wd", 
    ecosystem %in% c("NW", "SW") ~ "Wt",
    TRUE ~ NA
  )) %>% 
  mutate(site = 
  case_when(
    ecosystem == "BP" ~ 1,
    ecosystem == "SP" ~ 2,
    ecosystem == "NW" ~ 1,
    ecosystem == "SW" ~ 2,
    ecosystem == "EW" ~ 1,
    ecosystem == "WW" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ NA
  )) %>% 
  select(gas, date, cover, site, transect, rep, flux, p.value, soil_moisture, soil_temperature)
```

# Flux QC 

**Logic table:**

Situation,                              CO2,  CH4,  N2O
CO2 p > 0.05 or CO2 flux > 9*,           NA,   NA,   NA
"CO2 is good, but CH4/N2O p > 0.05",    keep, 0,    0
CO2 is good and CH4/N2O p ≤ 0.05,       keep, keep, keep

*Set very high woodland CO2 emissions (> 9) related to ant burrow to `NA`

```{r flux-qc}
data <- data %>%
  group_by(date, cover, site, transect, rep) %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract the CO2 values for this chamber measurement
    co2_p     = p.value[gas == "co2"][1],
    co2_flux  = flux[gas == "co2"][1],
    
    # Flag bad analytical process / injection based on CO2
    bad_injection = (is.na(co2_p) | co2_p > 0.05) | 
                    (!is.na(co2_flux) & co2_flux > 9)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    flux = case_when(
      # Everything from a bad injection becomes NA
      bad_injection ~ NA_real_,
      
      # CO2 that passed the checks keeps its value
      gas == "co2" ~ flux,
      
      # CH4 / N2O with non-significant slope → 0 (only if injection was good)
      gas %in% c("ch4", "n2o") & p.value > 0.05 ~ 0,
      
      # Otherwise keep the calculated flux
      TRUE ~ flux
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-co2_p, -co2_flux, -bad_injection) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
coords <- read_csv("2022-site-coords.csv")
data %>%
  mutate(site = as.character(site)) %>% 
  unite(site, cover, site, sep = "-") %>% 
  left_join(coords) %>% 
  write_csv("2022-nachusa-fluxes.csv")
```

```{r detection-limit}
# ============================================================
# Lowest Detectable Flux for CH4 and N2O
# ============================================================

# ---- Instrument precision ----
ch4_std_ppm    <- 10.1      # ppm
n2o_std_ppm    <- 1.0       # ppm
rel_precision  <- 0.02      # 2%

ch4_precision_ppm <- ch4_std_ppm * rel_precision   # 0.303 ppm
n2o_precision_ppm <- n2o_std_ppm * rel_precision   # 0.030 ppm

# ---- Chamber parameters ----
area_m2   <- 0.05          # m²
height_m  <- 0.12          # m
time_min  <- 30            # minutes
time_s    <- time_min * 60

# ---- Ideal gas conversion (ppm → nmol m⁻³) ----
# At 1 atm and 25 °C:
# 1 ppm = 40.87 µmol m⁻³ = 40870 nmol m⁻³
R <- 0.082057              # L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹
T <- 298.15                # K
P <- 1                     # atm

moles_per_m3     <- (P / (R * T)) * 1000          # mol m⁻³
ppm_to_nmol_m3   <- moles_per_m3 * 1000           # nmol m⁻³ per ppm
# ≈ 40870

# ---- Minimum detectable flux ----
# F (nmol m⁻² s⁻¹) = (ΔC_nmol_m3 / Δt_s) * height_m

ch4_min_flux <- (ch4_precision_ppm * ppm_to_nmol_m3 / time_s) * height_m
n2o_min_flux <- (n2o_precision_ppm * ppm_to_nmol_m3 / time_s) * height_m

# ---- Results ----
cat("=== Lowest Detectable Flux ===\n")
cat(sprintf("CH4 precision          : %.3f ppm\n", ch4_precision_ppm))
cat(sprintf("CH4 lowest detectable flux : %.3f nmol m⁻² s⁻¹\n\n", ch4_min_flux))

cat(sprintf("N2O precision          : %.3f ppm\n", n2o_precision_ppm))
cat(sprintf("N2O lowest detectable flux : %.3f nmol m⁻² s⁻¹\n", n2o_min_flux))

cat("\nAssumptions used:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Chamber area     = %.3f m²\n", area_m2))
cat(sprintf("  Chamber height   = %.2f m\n", height_m))
cat(sprintf("  Deployment time  = %.0f min\n", time_min))
cat("  Temperature/pressure ≈ 25 °C, 1 atm\n")
```

## Q1b. What is the center and spread of each flux, for each cover type, over the growing season?
- data were not normally distributed, except for N2O
- therefore, report min, q25, median, q75, max 
- mean and standard deviation for N2O
- by-site for CH4, aggregated for CO2 and N2O 

```{r flux-dist, fig.width=8, fig.height=3}
data %>% 
  mutate(gas = fct_relevel(gas, "co2", "ch4", "n2o")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(flux, fill = cover)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~gas, 
             scales = "free",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(
    co2 = "CO[2]",
    ch4 = "CH[4]",
    n2o = "N[2]*O"
  ), label_parsed)) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = expression(atop("GHG Flux", "("*mu*"mol CO"[2]*" m"^{-2}*" s"^{-1}*"), (nmol CH"[4]*" | N"[2]*"O m"^{-2}*" s"^{-1}*")")),
       y = "Density",
       fill = "Cover") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "magma") +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(),
    size = 12,
    face = "bold"
  )
ggsave("paper-figures/fig2.png", height = 3, width = 8)
```

CO2 fluxes for woodlands are unimodal and peak at 2-3 (smallest source)
  (note, identified and removed outlier co2 flux in woodlands > 9)
CO2 flues for wetlands and prairie are bimodal with peaks at 1.5 and 4 (larger sources)

CH4 fluxes for woodlands are bimodal with peaks at -1.5 and 0 (largest sink)
CH4 fluxes for wetlands are bimodal with peaks at 1 and 0 (medium sink)
CH4 fluxes for prairie are bimodal with peaks at 0.6 and 9 (weakest sink)

N2O fluxes for all cover types are unimodal around zero, with slightly positive skew, esp for prairie

```{r co2-decision-tree}
d <- data %>%
  filter(gas == "co2") %>%
  mutate(
    cover = factor(cover),
    site = factor(site)
  ) %>%
  select(flux, soil_temperature, soil_moisture, cover) %>%
  na.omit()
tree_mod <- rpart(
  flux ~ soil_temperature + soil_moisture + cover,
  data = d,
  method = "anova",
  control = rpart.control(
    cp = 0.01,
    minsplit = 10,
    minbucket = 5
  )
)

# summary(tree_mod)
```

```{r co2-tree-eval}
# get best error
best_cp <- tree_mod$cptable[
  which.min(tree_mod$cptable[, "xerror"]),
  "CP"
]

best_cp

# prune tree
tree_pruned <- prune(tree_mod, cp = best_cp)

rpart.plot(tree_pruned)

printcp(tree_pruned)

# Training R²
pred <- predict(tree_pruned)
R2_train <- cor(d$flux, pred)^2

# Cross-validated R²
R2_cv <- 1 - min(tree_pruned$cptable[, "xerror"])

R2_train; R2_cv

tree_pruned$variable.importance/244.0486
```

nsplits = 6
CO2 CV R2 = 1-0.28630 = 0.71
Rel. Err. = 0.18

## CO2 Tree Q10

```{r}
df <- tibble(
  grouping = c("10-15", "15-20","15-20", "20-25", "20-25"),
  co2_flux = c(1.1, 1.8, 2.5, 2.8, 4.1),
  data_percent = c(0.3, 0.23, 0.16, 0.08, 0.22)
) %>% 
  group_by(grouping) %>% 
  # rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(group_percent = sum(data_percent),
         group_wt = data_percent/group_percent,
         group_wt_co2 = group_wt*co2_flux)  %>% 
  summarize(group_wt_co2 = sum(group_wt_co2))

# Add midpoints
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    T_mid = case_when(
      grouping == "10-15" ~ 12.5,
      grouping == "15-20" ~ 17.5,
      grouping == "20-25" ~ 22.5
    )
  )

# 1. Interval-specific Q10
Q10_lower <- (df$group_wt_co2[2] / df$group_wt_co2[1]) ^ 2
Q10_upper <- (df$group_wt_co2[3] / df$group_wt_co2[2]) ^ 2

# 2. Overall Q10 (or regression)
Q10_overall <- df$group_wt_co2[3] / df$group_wt_co2[1]

fit <- lm(log(group_wt_co2) ~ T_mid, data = df)
Q10_fit <- exp(10 * coef(fit)["T_mid"])

# Results
tibble(
  interval = c("10-15 → 15-20", "15-20 → 20-25", "Overall / fitted (12.5–22.5 °C)"),
  Q10 = round(c(Q10_lower, Q10_upper, Q10_overall), 2)
)
```

# more within node stats (change tree by creating/re-creating `tree_pruned`)

```{r}
node_stats <- tree_pruned$frame %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("node") %>%
  filter(var == "<leaf>") %>%          # keep only terminal nodes
  mutate(
    n          = n,
    mean       = yval,                 # predicted value (node mean)
    sse        = dev,                  # sum of squared errors
    variance   = dev / n,              # population variance
    sd         = sqrt(dev / n),        # within-node standard deviation
    se         = sd / sqrt(n)          # standard error of the mean
  ) %>%
  select(node, n, mean, sd, se)

print(node_stats)
```

            total_precip = sum(daily_total_precip*25.4, na.rm = T))
